book.title: Wards of the State: The Long Shadow of American Foster Care

argument.statement: The foster care system fails vulnerable children and helps produce a foster care-to-prison pipeline, as illustrated through the accounts of former foster youth and related courtroom outcomes.

book.rationale: The book focuses on the impact of American foster care systems on society and culture, while also addressing historical and political contexts surrounding the issue.
book.summary: "Told through the stories of eight former foster youth, a jolting exploration of a broken system from an award-winning journalist Through the stories of eight former foster kids, Claudia Rowe illustrates exactly where, when, and how the system is failing the children that it parents. With accounts from psychologists to advocates to judges to the former foster children themselves, Wards of the State paves a road to reform by pulling back the curtain on the heartbreaking realities faced by children in a system that fails its most vulnerable youth. By the time Maryanne was 19 years old, she was on trial for murder. After having been in and out of the foster homes for nearly a decade, she was trafficked and assaulted, and ultimately pointed a gun at her assailant-and pulled the trigger. She fled, but with no family and no real friends, it didn't take long for the police to catch up with her. In court, the defense blamed not the traffickers, nor Maryanne, but the state itself-or rather, the foster care system, which turns the state into the parent of hundreds of thousands of children. The state of Washington didn't listen, but Claudia Rowe did. Wards of the State by journalist and author Claudia Rowe widens an eye-opening case from a true-crime lens to an exploration of the foster care-to-prison pipeline.
